title: Add cohort-aware changepoint detector and actionable regression reporter for CI
author: Liam Chen
release_notes:
- Add cohort-aware changepoint detector to evaluate prompt-set stability
- Emit actionable regression reports with prioritized remediation hints and stable/unstable flags
- Wire new reporter into CI so failing cohorts create an annotated failure ticket
description:
Motivation: We've seen intermittent prompt-set regressions that are localized to small cohorts (e.g., specialized domain prompts, long-form responses). Existing delta gates treat the entire prompt-set as a single signal and either over-alert or miss subtle but important shifts. This PR introduces a cohort-aware changepoint detector plus an "actionable regression reporter" that turns detected regressions into prioritized CI annotations and optional Linear tickets.

What this does: Implements a lightweight changepoint detection module that operates on per-cohort time-series (metric: composite score per prompt cohort). The detector uses a rolling median absolute deviation (MAD) baseline with an exponential window to be robust against transient spikes. When a changepoint is confidently detected, the reporter aggregates contributing prompts, computes per-prompt delta attribution, and emits: 1) CI annotation with top-5 contributing prompts and suggested mitigations (eg. reduce temperature, revert model variant, run targeted eval), 2) a compact JSON artifact for downstream triage jobs, and 3) an optional draft Linear ticket with prefilled context when configured.

Design notes and trade-offs: We prioritized interpretability over complex Bayesian models so the detector is deterministic and cheap for CI. The MAD+EWMA hybrid gives stable baselining for cohorts with sparse traffic. We intentionally cap per-cohort sensitivity to avoid noisy alerts; there's an adaptive floor tied to cohort sample size. The reporter runs as a CI step after eval-harness completes metric aggregation and is pluggable (via config) into existing CI pipelines and the dashboard ingestion pipeline.

Files changed (high-level):
- eval_harness/changepoint/detector.py (new) -- changepoint logic and unit tests
- eval_harness/reporters/actionable_reporter.py (new) -- reporter + CI annotation glue
- eval_harness/ci/steps.yaml (modified) -- add reporter as optional post-eval step
- eval_harness/tests/test_changepoint.py (new) -- coverage for detector edge cases
- scripts/ci/create_linear_stub.py (new small utility) -- optional ticket creation helper (feature gated)
- docs/eval/ci-changepoint.md (new) -- short ops runbook and configuration reference
- integrations/metrics/schema_v2.json (tweak) -- add cohort stability fields

Commits (summary):
- Initial skeleton and baseline MAD/EWMA implementation
- Add unit tests and sample cohort fixtures
- Wire reporter into CI step and add artifact output format
- Add doc and runbook; fix race condition in ticket creation helper

Testing performed:
- Unit tests for detector on synthetic cohorts (sparse, bursty, drifty) included; CI coverage >= 88% for the new modules.
- Integration test run on a snapshot of production eval data (sanitized) to validate false positive rate < 2% for cohorts with >50 samples in a week.
- End-to-end smoke in a staging CI pipeline with reporter producing annotations and artifacts.

Checklist: [x] Unit tests added [x] Integration smoke tested in staging [x] Docs updated [x] Config knobs documented [ ] Feature gated by default in org-level CI (will enable via rollout flag)

Backward compatibility and rollout: The change is off by default for org CI; individual repos can opt-in via eval_harness/ci/steps.yaml. Schema additions to metrics are additive and backward compatible. The Linear ticket creation helper is disabled unless API creds are provided via CI secrets.

Review notes: reviewers should focus on the sensitivity/default thresholds in detector.py and the phrasing in CI annotations (we want helpful guidance without prescriptive answers). The reporter's artifact JSON is intentionally compact to avoid large CI logs; if reviewers prefer more verbose output we can add an optional --verbose flag.

Merge: Squash and merge after approvals. Post-merge: I will run a staged rollout to 10% of org repos and monitor alert volume for 48 hours.
review_comments: Anita Sharma: The MAD baseline looks reasonable, but can we expose the sensitivity multiplier as a config flag? Some teams will want tighter thresholds.
Author(Liam Chen): Exposed sensitivity_multiplier and min_samples threshold; defaults chosen to match current internal heuristics. Added tests for multiplier=0.8/1.5/2.0.
Diego Morales: CI annotation content needs to avoid leaking model internals — can you sanitize model ids?
Author(Liam Chen): Sanitization added; model ids are now hashed in the annotation payload and full ids only go to the artifact JSON (protected by CI artifact access controls).
Sofia Patel: Concerned about ticket spam if many small cohorts trigger — what's the dedupe strategy?
Author(Liam Chen): Implemented a 24-hour dedupe window keyed by cohort+metric signature; documented behavior in runbook.
merge_comment: Merged after approvals from Anita and Diego. Staged rollout plan recorded in PR.
